# Client documentation site: project rules

Status: the local build with Zensical 0.1.3 was `verified` on macOS (2026-11-27). Publishing to GitHub Pages is `unverified`.

## Build

- Content: Markdown in `docs/cliente/`, in Portuguese, for people who use the data.
- Config: `mkdocs.yml` at the repository root, with `docs_dir: docs/cliente` and `site_dir: site`.
- Tool: the version pinned in `requirements-docs.txt`. Check: `zensical build --clean --strict`. Preview: `zensical serve`.
- `site/` is generated and ignored by Git.

## Pages

Start, source and licence, what is in the data, quality and limitations, indicators, changelog. Take facts from code, read-only queries (skill `databricks-sql-query`) or the cited source, with the date. Mark what does not exist yet as planned. Do not invent numbers.

## Never publish

Logs, internal errors, agent instructions, teaching material, workspace addresses, identities or personal data. Never set `docs_dir` to `docs/` or the repository root.

## Publish to GitHub Pages

Publishing is a write outside the machine: follow `write-contract`.

- A GitHub Actions workflow builds the site and deploys it, so readers and authors need no local publishing tool. Read the current official GitHub Pages and Zensical publishing instructions before writing it. Do not guess action names or versions.
- Deploy only on push to `main`, after a reviewed pull request. Pull requests only build.
- Upload only `site/`. Give the deploy job only the permissions it needs.
- One-time repository setting, done by the user: Settings, Pages, source "GitHub Actions".
- A site published from a public repository on a personal account is public.

## Done

The workflow is green and the public address opens in a private browser window. Check menu, search, diagrams and links there, and search the published pages for internal terms. Report the address.
